fillet_flight.prompt:
Production sprite atlas for Fight Guild: FILLET neutral jump and air-dash transitions, following her already approved movement contract. Use attached images as strict identity and anatomy references, especially reference1 for in-air proportions and knife ownership, reference2 for her wide Stalker ground stance. Exactly SIX full-body drawings in a regular 3-column x 2-row grid on a true transparent background. Each cell has equal dimensions, identical drawing scale, generous clear gutter. Character faces RIGHT in every frame. Black short swept-back hair, slender arms, pale rolled blouse, single red shoulder plate on anatomical LEFT arm (viewer right/front), crimson corset, brown trousers, brown gold-buckled boots, torn white/red apron. LONG knife in anatomical RIGHT bare-shoulder hand (viewer left/back); SHORT knife in anatomical LEFT red-shoulder hand near chest. Keep head size, torso, boots and costume identical. No trails, no smears, no glow, no captions, no arrows, no ground, no shadows. Fixed camera, orthographic game side-three-quarter view. These are neutral body poses, NOT attacks: knives stay safely near the guard.
Six poses in reading order: 1 TAKEOFF/FAST ASCENT: launched from a wide crouch, body extending, rear leg trails downward and front knee beginning to fold, spine lifted; 2 SLOW ASCENT: legs gather toward the compact guarded pose in reference1, knees visibly separated; 3 APEX/NEUTRAL GUARD: closely match the first or last pose of reference1 with one thigh folded and other boot lower, relaxed guarded knives, lowest vertical speed; 4 EARLY DESCENT: same upper body and pelvis size as3, toes opening downward, knees beginning to extend with leading leg lower, preparing to land; 5 LATE DESCENT: both legs reach toward the ground to find the wide staggered Stalker landing, torso leans forward slightly, bent soft knees, do not stretch torso; 6 AIR DASH BURST: strong compact forward torso lean with both legs trailing rear-left, upper body stays in guarded position, no slash or smear. Make distinct leg silhouettes between ascent and descent, physical weight transfer and compact torso, no excessive tumbling. All poses same physical body size; do not fit compact poses by enlarging them. Align pelvis positions similarly in each cell; preserve entire boot and knife tips. Clean cel-shaded anime fighting game production art with crisp dark contours matching references. Output transparent RGBA.

fillet_ground.prompt:
Create a production game sprite atlas of FILLET from these approved references, for grounded JUMP PREPARATION and LANDING only. Strict identity: black swept-back hair, lean slim arms, white rolled blouse, crimson corset and one red shoulder on anatomical LEFT, long knife anatomical RIGHT bare-shoulder hand, short knife LEFT near chest; matching boots, belts, apron, anatomy and cel shading. SIX full body frames, 3 columns x 2 rows, equal cells, true transparent background with no shadow, no text, no dividers. Character faces RIGHT throughout. This is the same compact athletic fighter at constant anatomical scale, not six new designs. All grounded drawings use EXACT SAME FOOT CONTACT LOCATIONS and same stance width as the wide Stalker pose in reference1; preserve knife hand ownership. No camera changes. No effects, no automatic smear, no interpolation ghosting.
Read left to right: TOP row is TAKEOFF: 1 the reference1 wide Stalker guard nearly identical; 2 lower pelvis and flex both knees to compress for jump, only about 10 percent lower head, feet firmly at reference1 positions, short knife remains guarding near chin; 3 driving through legs with both heels beginning to rise, torso and neck extended upwards a little, preparing airborne ascent, still both toes on ground. BOTTOM row is LANDING: 4 same wide feet at same contact points, knees flexed and torso tilts forward to absorb landing, both knives guarded, about 15 percent compression; 5 knees extend halfway back to the reference Stalker pose, chest rises but FOOT POSITIONS DO NOT SLIDE; 6 return exactly to reference1 Stalker guard. Every frame must fit with generous clear gutters and full weapons/feet visible. Keep the same head and limb size in bent and extended poses. Rhythm is held load then takeoff, and quick landing absorption then return; avoid stiff upright standing. Anatomy and costume from reference2 in air should be consistent with this ground set.

hammer_options.prompt:
Create a polished fighting-game animation direction study for HAMMER using the attached approved character sheet as the exact identity reference. This is a NEW approval board, not a production sprite sheet. Preserve the bald dark-skinned muscular man, blue scarf, white/silver armour, cream tabard with blue crossed-hammer emblem, brown boots, same warhammer, mature small head, heavy anatomy, clean cel-shaded inked style. Keep weapon low and close as in the approved compact Shoulder Drive stance. Side view facing right throughout.

Landscape board, two clearly separated horizontal rows, THREE large full-body sequential poses PER row. Dark desaturated blue-grey background, faint floor baseline and simple ivory typography. No particle effects or smears. Strong anatomical consistency and constant scale. Do not let arrows cover the legs.
Title: "HAMMER / FOOTWORK OPTIONS".
Row A label "A — GROUNDED MARCH". Three poses show LEFT leg leading contact -> right leg passing while left supports body -> RIGHT leg leading contact. Small knee compression, controlled shoulder bob, heavy heel-to-toe weight transfer, feet neither cross nor hop. Low hammer stays near hips; weapon and torso do not change size. Thin gold arrows beneath show foot motion and short down/up pelvis arrows. Number the poses 1 / 2 / 3.
Row B label "B — PRESSURE SHUFFLE". Three poses show lead left foot reaches -> rear right foot gathers under hips -> lead foot resets forward. Lower crouched torso, shorter sliding steps, upper-body almost level and hammer braced close. Distinguish it visibly from A. The lead foot remains nearest the opponent, no cross step. Direction arrows on travel/heel paths. Number 1 / 2 / 3.
Both rows should read as a movement timeline, not three unrelated action portraits. Full hammer and boots fit inside every panel, generous gutters. This choice will guide walk, retreat and the matching run; don't show attacks. Use accurate weight, opposing shoulder/hip rotation, flexible knee/ankle mechanics rather than stiff cutout figures.
